evidence: The core issue arises when a user—especially a **MEV bot—stakes a huge amount of HYPE** just before the `ValidatorManager` injects new rewards into the system. At this point, the exchange ratio is still low. As a result, the user receives more kHYPE tokens than they would if the reward had already been distributed. Once the reward is deposited, the total HYPE in the system increases, and so does the value of each kHYPE token. If the attacker now withdraws their position (or queues a withdrawal), they receive more HYPE than they initially staked, effectively capturing an unfair portion of the newly added rewards.
